propositions: The complexity lock compares branch baselines against main tip instead of merge-base, causing unrebased branches to fail when main lowers a ceiling even if the branch made no changes to complexity
Any ceiling reduction on main breaks all open changes that have not rebased, falsely reporting a ceiling raise on the branch when the change was made on main
The lock must compare against merge-base(main, HEAD) and read the baseline at that commit so only entries the branch itself changed can trigger a violation
When a merge base cannot be computed the lock must fall back to main-tip comparison with explicit notification, preserving fail-closed behavior
The fetch of main baseline uses --depth=1 which is too shallow to compute merge bases and must be deepened, and shallow checkouts must be unshallowed before computing the merge base
